source.title: Unveiling Privacy, Memorization, and Input Curvature Links
source.authors: Deepak Ravikumar; Efstathia Soufleri; Abolfazl Hashemi; Kaushik Roy

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper empirically measures the association between input loss curvature and stability-based memorization, and how differential privacy changes curvature and memorization. These are related measurements bearing on V7 and V8, but use different methods and do not test the versions' specified generalization-gap or example-removal outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper's experiments on curvature versus memorization and privacy versus curvature/memorization bear on V7 and V8. Results it cites about prior work, including the claimed compute savings and Figure 2 examples, are not rows. No experiment tests the architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, or width comparisons in V1–V6.
record.test_reason: The study measures input loss curvature, per-example memorization, and differential privacy. It does not measure V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness versus generalization gap or V8's test-accuracy loss after removing highly memorized versus random examples. Its other results and theoretical arguments do not test V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase broadly captures the authors' conclusion, but overstates uniform empirical tightness. They derive conditional upper bounds linking memorization, input curvature, and privacy, and report strong empirical agreement on CIFAR and ImageNet. Curvature fits use empirically modeled loss bounds, while measured memorization remains substantially below the privacy-based upper bound.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops theoretical bounds and measures input loss curvature, memorization scores, and differential-privacy effects; it does not reproduce the original methods specified by the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The curvature–memorization linearity weakens at extreme data-range ends, especially on ImageNet; assuming a sub-population-dependent loss bound improves the fitted match. Curvature estimator results were reported robust to the tested changes in step size h and number of Rademacher vectors n.

fits_no_version.finding: Binned memorization scores and input curvature show a strong linear trend for Small Inception on CIFAR100 and ResNet50 on ImageNet, with deviations at the extremes. A fitted sub-population-dependent loss bound improves agreement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these pretrained model ensembles, maximum input curvature per memorization bin is associated with average stability-based memorization; the fitted relationship depends on modeling the loss bound.

fits_no_version.finding: Estimated memorization of the selected top-500 CIFAR100 examples increases with privacy budget and remains well below the stated theoretical upper bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the selected examples and tested ResNet18 DP-SGD settings, weaker privacy guarantees accompany greater estimated own-label memorization.

fits_no_version.finding: Average input curvature versus privacy budget closely matches the fitted theoretical model on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100, using an empirically modeled privacy-dependent loss bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Average input curvature in these private ResNet18 models varies with privacy budget in agreement with the study's fitted curvature–privacy model.

record.code_released: Code provided in supplementary material; URL not stated.
record.problems: No uncertainty intervals or statistical tests are stated for the empirical relationships. The primary curvature–memorization evidence is presented in figures and bin-level aggregates; the text says the linear trend weakens at extreme data-range ends. The authors' improved fits rely on empirically modeled loss bounds. The privacy–memorization experiment covers selected top-500 examples and does not report a random-example comparison or test accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying result rows identified. Figure 2's low- and high-curvature example images and the stated efficiency comparison reproduce or describe prior work and are not this study's own measured outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label held-out generalization and chance performance on random-label test data.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning and optimizer recipe changes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps across networks with similarly low training loss, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Held-out accuracy after removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Using Feldman–Zhang checkpoints, memorization scores, and selected examples does not test their example-removal generalization result. Generalization is also an assumption of the curvature theorems, rather than an experimentally established outcome here.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence across the specified models and settings.
Test error as network width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the stated local-connectivity comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons and tuning or recipe changes.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.

No comparison of magnitude-aware sharpness with norm- and margin-based measures; no perturbation-tolerance ranking across trained networks. The experiment instead relates input loss curvature to stability-based memorization scores.

No removal and retraining comparison against removing random examples; no test-accuracy outcome for that intervention. The experiment instead varies differential privacy and estimates memorization scores of selected examples.

rows.subject: Small Inception
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR100; end of training
rows.operation_detail: Compared input loss curvature scores with stability-based memorization scores, averaged across 1000 models and binned by memorization score.
rows.measure: Relationship between average memorization score and maximum curvature score per bin.
rows.value: The authors report a clear linear relation and a strong linear trend; a sub-population loss-bound fit improved the match.
rows.locator: Section 6.3, Figure 3(a), and Accounting for Variables in Practice
rows.note: Curvature is the paper's proxy/theoretical counterpart to memorization, not magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness or the training–test gap. The paper notes linearity diminishes at extreme data-range ends and its improved fit assumes a changing loss bound.
rows.check: Input curvature versus per-example memorization cannot establish V7's weight-perturbation sharpness versus training–test gap. The reported linear trend is outside the version.
